blocks.content: Glaciers carve distinct U-shaped valleys through plucking and abrasion, whereas rivers carve steep V-shaped valleys through fluvial downcutting.

rows: U-shaped valley with flat floor and steep walls
V-shaped valley with narrow bottom and sloping sides
Cirques, Arêtes, Horns, Hanging Valleys, Fjords
Alluvial Fans, Deltas, Oxbow Lakes, Levees

items: Competitive exams frequently test classification: Moraines, Eskers, and Drumlins are depositional glacial features, whereas Cirques and Arêtes are erosional.
Drumlins are inverted boat-shaped hills composed of unsorted till, commonly described as 'basket of eggs topography'.
Hanging valleys are formed by tributary glaciers and often create dramatic waterfalls where they meet the main valley.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Glaciers create flat-bottomed, steep-sided U-shaped valleys through ice plucking and abrasion.
Rivers carve steep-sided V-shaped valleys mainly through vertical downcutting and hydraulic erosion.
Cirques, hanging valleys, horns, and arêtes are primary erosional glacial landforms.
Drumlins, eskers, and moraines are depositional glacial landforms, with drumlins forming a 'basket of eggs' topography.
Deltas, meanders, oxbow lakes, and alluvial fans represent typical fluvial (river) depositional landforms.
